data.description: Ultra-compressed communication mode. Shortens prose while preserving technical terms, code, commands, and exact errors.

publications.verifiedBy: The marketplace "caveman" is defined in the same repository by .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (source "./"); .claude-plugin/plugin.json names the plugin "caveman" at version 4.1.0.

supportedUseCases.title: Make agent replies terse
supportedUseCases.description: The caveman, ultracave and megacave skills cut filler and keep technical terms, code, commands and exact errors.

supportedUseCases.title: Write terse Conventional Commit messages
supportedUseCases.description: The caveman-commit skill compresses a commit message to intent only.

supportedUseCases.title: Review a diff with one line per finding
supportedUseCases.description: The caveman-review skill gives location, problem and fix for each finding.

supportedUseCases.title: Compress a memory file such as CLAUDE.md
supportedUseCases.description: The caveman-compress skill rewrites the file in caveman format and keeps a readable backup outside the source tree.

supportedUseCases.title: Show recorded token usage for the current session
supportedUseCases.description: The caveman-stats skill reports output and cache-read tokens and mode attribution.

supportedUseCases.title: Delegate code lookup, small edits and review to compressed subagents
supportedUseCases.description: The cavecrew skill and three cavecrew subagents keep the main context small.

supportedUseCases.title: Apply a task-shaped work pattern
supportedUseCases.description: Six skills shape how the agent investigates, builds, patches, refactors, migrates and verifies.

supportedUseCases.title: Observe and reduce LLM spend with Caveman Cloud and the Caveman CLI
supportedUseCases.description: The setup, discover, evidence-review, manage, optimize and learn skills drive Caveman Cloud and the CLI.

interfaces.description: Claude Code plugin. plugin.json declares four hooks; skills/, agents/ and commands/ at the plugin root are auto-discovered.
22 Agent Skills under skills/, loaded by name and description. Five have their own manifests (components); 17 are listed in embeddedComponents.

runtime.detail: Loaded as a plugin; the plugin root is the repository root.
Node.js on PATH for the four hooks; Python 3 for the scripts of the caveman-compress skill.

setup.name: CAVEMAN_DEFAULT_MODE
setup.description: Optional. Default mode at session start: off, caveman, ultracave, megacave, commit, review, compress, or manual. Without it, a repo-local .caveman/config.json or .caveman.json, then the user config, then caveman.

setup.name: CAVEMAN_REINFORCE
setup.description: Optional. Per-turn reinforcement switch, on by default. Also settable as "reinforce" in the config files.

setup.name: CAVE_API_KEY
setup.description: Only for the caveman-setup skill. The Caveman Cloud gateway auth secret; keep it in an environment variable and never commit it.

limitations: Every skills/*/SKILL.md ships to every plugin user with no allowlist, so all 22 skill descriptions compete for activation on ordinary work.
Saves nothing on agents billed per request, such as GitHub Copilot. The rules add input tokens, and the project's own notes list cases where caveman is net-negative.
Output reduction against an "Answer concisely." control is 3% (caveman), 35% (ultracave) and 9% (megacave) at the median; n=10, one run, measured on the 3.1.0 skill text.
The caveman-compress skill sends the full text of the named file to the model provider its script is configured for (claude CLI, Anthropic API or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint) and needs python3.

The caveman-setup, -discover, -manage, -optimize and -evidence-review skills serve Caveman Cloud, a separate commercial service. Setup needs CAVE_API_KEY; manage, optimize and evidence-review need a Caveman CLI login.
The caveman-learn skill acts on the output of `caveman learn report --json`, which needs the Caveman CLI.
The four hooks run node and exit silently when Node.js is not on PATH, so session activation, mode tracking and stats recording do not run without it.

costInformation.details: The repository is Apache-2.0. Caveman Cloud, which several driver skills target, is separate commercial software that this license does not cover.

embeddedComponents.name: cavecrew
embeddedComponents.description: When to delegate to `cavecrew-investigator` (locate code), `cavecrew-builder` (1-2 file edit) or `cavecrew-reviewer` (diff review) instead of working inline or using `Explore`. Their output is compressed, so main context lasts longer.

embeddedComponents.name: caveman-compress
embeddedComponents.description: Compress a memory file such as CLAUDE.md or a todo list into caveman format to save input tokens, keeping a readable backup. Sends the file's text to the configured model provider. Trigger: /caveman-compress.

embeddedComponents.name: caveman-help
embeddedComponents.description: Quick-reference card for the three caveman skills and their commands. Trigger: /caveman-help or "caveman help".

embeddedComponents.name: caveman-stats
embeddedComponents.description: Show recorded output and cache-read token usage and mode attribution for the current Claude Code session, or locate the host's native usage report. Trigger: /caveman-stats.

embeddedComponents.name: caveman-setup
embeddedComponents.description: Wire a repository through the Caveman Cloud gateway so every LLM request is measured, with no behavior change. Use for "set up caveman" or adding LLM spend observability.

embeddedComponents.name: caveman-discover
embeddedComponents.description: Find and label every LLM workflow in the repository so Caveman Cloud groups spend by workflow instead of one bucket. Use for "discover workflows" or breaking LLM spend down by workflow.

embeddedComponents.name: caveman-learn
embeddedComponents.description: Act on a Caveman learn report - review the ranked token sinks, apply cost-lowering fixes with per-edit consent, and report what those fixes returned. Use when asked to lower an agent's token cost, what caveman has saved, to trim a heavy CLAUDE.md, or to offload re-pasted context into cavemem.

embeddedComponents.name: caveman-manage
embeddedComponents.description: Inspect Caveman Cloud's experiment lifecycle and block unsafe execution. Use when asked to start, approve, cancel, promote or roll back a Caveman experiment.

embeddedComponents.name: caveman-optimize
embeddedComponents.description: Turn a Caveman optimization observation into an operator-chosen candidate with a paired baseline evaluation. Use when asked to inspect or evaluate a Caveman optimization report. Needs explicit approval.

embeddedComponents.name: caveman-explore
embeddedComponents.description: Read-only repository explorer for cold-start orientation, broad cross-file localization, or when a direct search failed. Skip it when the exact file or symbol is already named. Returns path:line citations only; its reads stay out of main context.

embeddedComponents.name: caveman-evidence-review
embeddedComponents.description: Read-only review of Caveman Cloud evidence: cost, Cave Score, workflows, traces, latency, errors, routing, savings. Use when asked what Caveman found or where LLM spend goes.

embeddedComponents.name: investigate-first
embeddedComponents.description: Diagnose ambiguous failures before editing. Use for unknown causes, intermittent behavior, performance regressions, or investigations needing evidence-ranked hypotheses.

embeddedComponents.name: lean-build
embeddedComponents.description: Build feature work with high overbuilding risk. Use for new behavior, product slices, or integrations where repository reuse, strict scope, and an explicit stop condition matter.

embeddedComponents.name: surgical-patch
embeddedComponents.description: Fix bugs and small behavior changes at the narrowest responsible layer. Use when regression proof, preserved surrounding behavior, and task-relevant tests matter.

embeddedComponents.name: safe-refactor
embeddedComponents.description: Restructure code while preserving behavior. Use for extraction, consolidation, ownership moves, or cleanup where verification must bracket structural edits.

embeddedComponents.name: migration
embeddedComponents.description: Implement reversible compatibility-safe transitions. Use for schema, data, API, protocol, configuration, or dependency migrations requiring rollback and preservation proof.

embeddedComponents.name: verify-and-stop
embeddedComponents.description: Prove existing work meets acceptance conditions without expanding scope. Use for validation-only tasks, completion checks, focused gate runs, and last-mile proof.

embeddedComponents.name: cavecrew-investigator
embeddedComponents.description: Read-only code locator. Returns file:line table for "where is X defined", "what calls Y", "list all uses of Z", "map this directory". Output is caveman-compressed, one row per hit, to keep main-thread context small. Refuses to suggest fixes.

embeddedComponents.name: cavecrew-reviewer
embeddedComponents.description: Diff/branch/file reviewer. One line per finding, severity-tagged, no praise, no scope creep. Output format `path:line: <emoji> <severity>: <problem>. <fix>.` Use for "review this PR", "review my diff", "audit this file". Skips formatting nits unless they change meaning.

embeddedComponents.name: caveman-init
embeddedComponents.description: Drop the always-on caveman activation rule into the current repo for every IDE agent

embeddedComponents.name: SessionStart
embeddedComponents.description: Runs src/hooks/caveman-activate.js (timeout 30 s). Status message "Loading caveman mode...".

embeddedComponents.name: SubagentStart
embeddedComponents.description: Runs src/hooks/caveman-activate.js --subagent (timeout 30 s). Status message "Loading caveman mode for subagent...".

embeddedComponents.name: UserPromptSubmit
embeddedComponents.description: Runs src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js (timeout 30 s). Status message "Tracking caveman mode...".

embeddedComponents.name: SessionEnd
embeddedComponents.description: Runs src/hooks/caveman-stats.js --record (timeout 5 s). Status message "Recording caveman stats...".

publications.verifiedBy: The README's Claude Code plugin instructions; the plugin installs the MCP server and its skills.

Performance tools may send trace URLs to the Google CrUX API unless run with --no-performance-crux.

The README's configuration uses the floating @latest version; pin a version for production.

entries.description: Open-source Python library that converts PDFs, HTML, Word documents, images, and many other formats into structured elements (titles, text, tables) for language models. Partitions PDFs with layout detection and OCR, including table extraction.

data.name: Unstructured
data.description: Open-source Python library that converts PDFs, HTML, Word documents, images, and many other formats into structured elements (titles, text, tables) for language models. Partitions PDFs with layout detection and OCR, including table extraction.

publications.verifiedBy: Documented in the README's Quick Start; images are built for every push to main.

relations.evidence: The README separates the open-source library from Unstructured's enterprise Platform product.

supportedUseCases.title: Extract text and tables from PDFs
supportedUseCases.description: partition_pdf returns the document's elements, including tables, using layout detection and OCR.

supportedUseCases.title: Prepare documents for language models
supportedUseCases.description: Turns many document formats into clean elements for chunking and embedding.

interfaces.description: Python API, for example unstructured.partition.pdf.partition_pdf.

inputs.description: The PDF to partition; other formats are supported with extras.

runtime.detail: Python >=3.11,<3.14; PDF support needs the pdf extra (or all-docs).

setup.description: Set to any non-empty value to turn off the library's analytics, which are on by default (SCARF_NO_ANALYTICS works too).

limitations: Sends analytics pings to packages.unstructured.io by default (no document content, per the README); set DO_NOT_TRACK to opt out.
PDF processing needs system packages (poppler, tesseract) as well as the Python extras.
